why: A black hole with a glowing ember rim and a lone candle burns through a sunset camp photo under a big serif 'HARRY POTTER' title. The burn is a strong 'what is it revealing?' pull. Caveat: the picture beneath is a Western camp, so the title and image disagree for a beat and it can read as a lag.

A cream-bordered sepia tintype of a valley with a drifting heat-haze band, with 'RED DEAD REDEMPTION 2' set large above it. It looks like an old photograph coming to life, is clear, calm, and gives a distinct sense of a new chapter.

A jagged torn-edge wipe, with a pale classroom on the left giving way to a stormy teal sea on the right, under the '3 IDIOTS' title. The motion and the tear are striking and cinematic. The pale left side is washed out and the sea is the previous world, so the mid-wipe frame is a little muddled.

A bright gold porthole ring on a near-black plate reveals a lantern-lit ghost ship, with a blackletter 'PIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN' title. The ring is a strong focal point and signals a reveal. Two thirds of the image is empty black, which weakens it.

The same porthole a moment later: the ring is thinner and dimmer, the ship is cropped, and the plate is almost entirely black. It looks like a dark rectangle with a small circle. Only the blackletter title carries it.

A glowing teal chart line sweeps across the bottom of a storm sea and reveals the classroom desk beneath it. It links the data idea to the film imagery, and the line gives the eye a direction. The sea and stone desk are only partly legible, though.

A jagged, glowing-rimmed hole in the camp photo now shows a blue night sky with a candle inside, suggesting a different world seeping in. Intriguing. Same title and image mismatch as H001, since 'HARRY POTTER' sits over a Western camp.

A desaturated, sepia valley with a soft sun glow, a haze band and thin arcs along the bottom, under a large 'RED DEAD REDEMPTION 2' title. Atmospheric and photographic. The frame border has gone, so it feels slightly less composed than H002, but it still pulls.
